Based on my knowledge of chemistry and hazardous materials classification, I can provide an answer to this question:

Aluminum phosphide (AlP) is known to react vigorously with water to produce phosphine gas (PH₃), which is highly toxic and flammable. When aluminum phosphide comes in contact with water or moisture, it produces phosphine gas according to the reaction:
AlP + 3H₂O → Al(OH)₃ + PH₃

Under the CLP Regulation [VO (EG) No. 1272/2008], substances that emit flammable gases when in contact with water are classified in a specific hazard category. Aluminum phosphide falls into this category because it releases phosphine gas, which is flammable, when it comes into contact with water.

Therefore, aluminum phosphide is classified according to CLP Regulation as a substance that emits flammable gases when in contact with water.
